items.stem: A Cloud Run service receives bursty traffic and each container can safely handle many simultaneous requests. To raise throughput most cost-effectively, what should you adjust first?

options.rationale: Correct: higher concurrency lets each instance serve more requests, reducing the instance count needed.

options.text: Lower concurrency to 1 and add more instances
options.rationale: This wastes resources and raises cost when containers can handle parallel requests.

options.text: Switch the service to a Compute Engine VM
options.rationale: That abandons the serverless model without addressing the concurrency setting.
Disabling autoscaling removes the mechanism that handles bursts.

items.explanation: Correct: higher concurrency lets each instance serve more requests, reducing the instance count needed.

items.stem: You are rolling out a risky change to a Cloud Run service. Which TWO actions support a safe, reversible release? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Deploy the change as a new revision and send it only a small traffic percentage
options.rationale: Correct: a canary limits exposure while you watch metrics.

options.text: Keep the previous revision available to roll back to
options.rationale: Correct: an intact prior revision makes rollback immediate.

options.text: Delete the previous revision immediately after deploying
options.rationale: Deleting it removes the rollback target.

options.text: Send 100% of traffic to the new revision at once
options.rationale: That is the opposite of a controlled canary.

items.explanation: Correct: both keyed options are right; the distractors are wrong for the reasons given.

items.stem: An internal Cloud Run API should be callable only from within the VPC and services should not use broad default credentials. Which configuration best meets this?

options.text: Set internal ingress and assign a dedicated least-privilege service account
options.rationale: Correct: internal ingress plus a scoped service account enforces both requirements.

options.text: Make the service public and rely on a password in the app
options.rationale: Public ingress exposes the service beyond the VPC.

options.text: Use the default service account with Owner role
options.rationale: Owner is far broader than least privilege.
Unauthenticated access contradicts the internal-only requirement.

items.explanation: Correct: internal ingress plus a scoped service account enforces both requirements.
